tables.how: Every provider number registered in San Francisco, service code and year in the federal file (37,870 combinations tested). A row is kept when the total paid is above the national 99th percentile for that service and year, the amount per claim line is at least three times the national median and at least one and a half times what other California billers averaged, with at least 100 claim lines, $100,000 and 50 billers nationwide; for a service with 15 to 49 billers nationwide the bar is $1 million and a quarter of everything California paid for it. That gives 126 service-years for 20 provider numbers, $1,076,014,633 in all. 7 numbers belong to City government or the University of California ($1,044,063,102); the other 13, the case's figure, were paid $31,951,531. The case page shows each provider once, on its largest service-year; this list has them all.
tables.limits: An outlier is a reason to look, not a finding, and no authority has made one about any provider listed. A claim line can carry many units: California counties bill mental health by the minute, and public clinics, health centers and City ambulances are paid cost-based rates set by the State, so a whole visit or session on one line looks like a high price. A specialty explains many gaps, and health plans report what they pay differently from the State. The file has no units, no diagnoses and nothing about any person treated. The federal file withholds every cell with fewer than 12 claim lines, so every total is a lower bound, and 2024 is preliminary. The address is where the provider is registered, not where care was given.

tables.how: Payments to each of the 829 billing numbers registered in San Francisco were added up by calendar year of service. Tripled (19 rows): at least $50,000 one year and at least three times that, and $500,000 or more, the next. Year by year: 2018: $439.5 million paid, 212,217 enrolled, $2,071 each against $1,150 for California (1.80 times), City government's share 70%; 2019: $335.3 million paid, 205,606 enrolled, $1,631 each against $1,218 for California (1.34 times), City government's share 61%; 2020: $344.0 million paid, 209,780 enrolled, $1,640 each against $1,226 for California (1.34 times), City government's share 56%; 2021: $420.2 million paid, 229,282 enrolled, $1,833 each against $1,312 for California (1.40 times), City government's share 51%; 2022: $430.3 million paid, 243,811 enrolled, $1,765 each against $1,272 for California (1.39 times), City government's share 53%; 2023: $556.5 million paid, 255,938 enrolled, $2,174 each against $1,482 for California (1.47 times), City government's share 51%; 2024: $465.2 million paid, 255,107 enrolled, $1,823 each against $1,468 for California (1.24 times), City government's share 44%. tables.limits: This compares where billers are registered, not where the people treated live. San Francisco hosts a university medical center, the City's own hospital and mental-health system and national laboratories that bill for people everywhere, so its figure is bound to be higher than the State's. Hospital stays, nursing homes and pharmacy are not in the file. Being paid by Medicaid is ordinary; nothing in this list is a sign of anything by itself.
